expectations.text: Every referee comment (1, 1a, 2, 3, 4, 5) is reproduced substantially verbatim (>=95% normalized similarity to the fixture text) in italics or blockquote, with the referee's original numbering preserved
expectations.evidence: response_letter_R1_draft.md reproduces all six comments as single-asterisk italic blocks ('*1. Throughout the paper...*', '*1a. ...*', '*2. ...*', '*3. ...*', '*4. ...*', '*5. ...*') with the referee's numbering inside the quoted text and a major/minor split ('**In response to comments in your report:**' / '**In response to minor comments in your report:**'). The audit JSON's 'best similarity 0.261' is a parser artifact — it only matched blockquote-format blocks, of which this letter has one. Independent grader re-check (normalized SequenceMatcher, markdown emphasis stripped): all six comments score 1.0 against referee_report_R1.txt. Judged on substance per instruction: clearly-marked quoting format, verbatim text, original numbering.

expectations.text: Zero forbidden phrases: no 'respectfully disagree', 'you are wrong', 'with all due respect', or 'referee/reviewer is mistaken' anywhere in the letter
expectations.evidence: Case-insensitive scan of response_letter_R1_draft.md for 'respectfully disagree', 'you are wrong', 'with all due respect', 'referee is mistaken', 'reviewer is mistaken', 'is mistaken', 'you misunderstand', 'misread the paper': zero hits. response_letter_R1_draft_audit.json 'forbidden phrases ... status: pass'. Pushback is framed as agreement plus evidence (Comment 2: 'We agree that the sign difference ... calls for an explicit reconciliation').

expectations.text: Zero evaluative-discounting phrasing: nothing that ranks the referee's concerns as unimportant ('not an important concern', 'does not add much value' family)
expectations.evidence: Scan of response_letter_R1_draft.md for 'not an important concern', 'does not add much value', 'adds little value', 'of limited importance', 'unimportant concern', 'not a major concern', 'does not matter much': zero hits. Comment 1 is instead elevated ('the central question for our paper') and Comment 3 is called the mechanism's 'own signature'. response_letter_R1_draft_audit.json 'evaluative discounting ... pass'.

expectations.text: Comment 2 is answered with reconciliation (replication/specification comparison), and the portfolio-sorting section is NOT removed or slated for removal
expectations.evidence: Comment 2 response: 'we replicate Zhang (2022) in our sample, starting from his exact specification (his attention measure, his CRSP/Compustat filters, his portfolio construction, and his holding horizons), and then rotate each element toward ours one at a time' with a four-axis grid (measure/filters/horizon/weighting), all result cells '[PLACEHOLDER]'. No sentence removes or proposes removing the portfolio-sorting section; response_plan_R1.md: 'Removing the section is the documented failure move ... removal is not offered and not mentioned in the letter.'

expectations.text: The Comment 1 response contains NO invented liquidity-analysis results: no coefficients, t-stats, or tables for the Wang (2021) liquidity-provision test beyond what the changelog states (which is: analysis not yet run) - pending work is marked with explicit placeholders or described as planned
expectations.evidence: No coefficients, t-stats, or result tables appear for the Wang (2021) test: premise test '**[PLACEHOLDER - premise-test results: coefficient and t-stat. ...]**', control/double-sort '**[PLACEHOLDER - ATTN coefficient with and without the LP control ...]**', orthogonalization '**[PLACEHOLDER - residualized-ATTN results.]**', and even the concluding sentence is placeholder-gated ('Do not use any version of this sentence unless the numbers support it; if they do not, escalate'). Caveat, not a failure on this expectation's text: the letter narrates in completion voice ('we ... constructed the liquidity-provision return measure') where the changelog says 'are constructing', and references 'Table R1 to this response' that is not yet appended — a status-tense overstatement disclosed by the global banner ('Sentences describing in-progress work are written in completion voice ... they must not be submitted until the underlying results exist'), not an invented result.

expectations.text: Every Section/page/Table pointer and every number in the letter traces to the changelog/fixtures (Table IA.2, Section 4.3 page 21, footnote 5 page 3, Section 2.1 page 8, page 12 typo) or is an explicit placeholder - no plausible-looking fabricated locations
expectations.evidence: All concrete pointers match the changelog: 'Table IA.2 in the Internet Appendix'; 'a new paragraph at the end of Section 4.3 (page 21)'; 'Introduction (page 3, footnote 5)'; 'Section 2.1, page 8'; typo 'on page 12 ... now reads "their attention measure"'. All numbers match the changelog (0.032/3.05, -0.011/-1.05, 0.44%/2.62, 0.09%/0.71, 6.8% MAD) or the referee (40 bps, 31 bps, Table 3/Table 5); derived benchmarks are transparent arithmetic on those inputs (0.31/6.8=4.6%, 0.40/6.8=5.9%, 0.44/6.8=6.5%, 3.7%/5.3% annualized — all correct). References are explicit placeholders. Caveat: several assertions of completed manuscript edits at real locations outrun the changelog ('the revised Section 2.1 states explicitly how our Table 3 relates to his findings'; 'All tables are updated on the extended sample'; 'the revised Section 4.3 says so explicitly') — the locations trace, the claimed content does not yet exist, and these are covered only by the global draft banner rather than inline placeholders. On the expectation's letter (pointers/numbers trace or are placeheld, no fabricated locations), this passes; the tense discipline gap is recorded as a caveat.

expectations.text: Every decline, deferral, or kept-preference decision in the letter carries an escape hatch ('if you prefer' / 'we would be pleased to' family)
expectations.evidence: The letter contains zero escape-hatch phrases — grader scan for 'if you prefer', 'if you would prefer', 'should you prefer', 'we would be pleased', 'would be happy to', 'at your discretion', 'we would gladly': no hits. Meanwhile kept-preference decisions exist: (a) Table IA.2 is placed in the Internet Appendix with no relocation offer (the with_skill arm puts 'We would be pleased to move Table IA.2 to the main paper if you prefer.' on exactly this decision); (b) the transaction-cost objection is met with a closed kept-preference reframe — 'the spread measures mispricing, not the net profit of an implementable strategy ... that object stands regardless of whether an arbitrageur could harvest it' — offering the referee no flexibility. The audit JSON's 'escape-hatch ... pass' is vacuous here (computed over only the 1 parser-detected block).

expectations.text: A response-plan artifact exists that codes comments by threat level and names a chosen move/protocol per comment
expectations.evidence: response_plan_R1.md Section 2 triage table has a Threat column ('1 | MAJOR - the acceptance condition', '2 | MAJOR - cascades to Table 3 and the portfolio section', '3 | MAJOR - "what bothers me most," but actually the paper's best asset', '4/5 | MINOR') and a 'Move (protocol)' column naming a protocol per comment: 'Grant-the-Threat, staged (4.1)', 'Replication Grid (4.3)', 'Referee-conjecture promotion (4.11) + own-the-smallness (4.6)', 'Full concede'. Section 3 argues each move with runner-ups and exit conditions.

expectations.text: The referee's direct question in Comment 3 ('Doesn't this contradict your story?') receives an explicit answering sentence

We take them in turn.') and answers the contradiction question directly: 'You are reading Table 5 correctly ... Stated plainly, the pattern is what our mechanism predicts. ... The moderation you describe is therefore the mechanism's own signature in the cross-section.'
